taxonomyNote: NatureServe's standard name is 'Dekay's Brownsnake' and notes some authors treat Storeria victa as a separate species; Missouri Department of Conservation says former subspecies are no longer recognised.
fieldMarks: Small, stout snake rarely over about 13-15 in; grayish-brown to reddish-brown with a lighter stripe down the back bordered by two rows of small dark spots.
Dark spot under each eye and on each side of the neck; heavily keeled scales (17 rows) and divided anal plate; belly cream, yellow or pink.
Young are black or dark gray with a light neck ring but keeled scales separate them from ring-necked snakes.
behavior: Secretive, hides under stones, boards and debris; most active late March to early November; often seen crossing roads in spring and fall.
Eats earthworms, slugs and snails (one study 75% slugs); specialised teeth help pull snails from their shells.
When threatened flattens its body and releases musk; gives birth to 3-41 young from mid-July to September.
habitat: Nearly all terrestrial and wetland habitat types including cities: moist forests, woodland edges along ravines and creeks, and grasslands near wetlands; hibernates underground or beneath buildings, often communally.
range: Eastern United States (east of the Rockies) and northern Mexico; in Canada southern Ontario and Quebec (NatureServe rank N5).

lookalikes.name: Ring-necked snake
lookalikes.howToTell: Young brown snakes have a pale neck ring but keeled scales, which ring-necked snakes lack (Animal Diversity Web).

lookalikes.name: Red-bellied snake
lookalikes.howToTell: Close relative with a tan back stripe bordered by two rows of small dark spots and a cream, yellow or pink belly, versus the red-bellied snake's red, orange or pink belly and three light nape spots (Missouri Department of Conservation).
